objects.content: The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. Le Monde's report that the defrost operation was lengthened from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late, and SecurityWeek's figure of about 700 supermarkets, the prosecutor's report of fires and the absence of a claim or ransom demand, are added, with Cybersecurity Dive's report that Copeland confirmed the flaw was found in discontinued controllers.

Check Point's sk1000171 lists R82.20 as affected without an 'all takes' scope; the qualifier is removed from the affected-version record and the analysis. The R82.20 Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator from Take 10 also carries the fix, and the end-of-support statement follows what sk1000171 lists. The detection paragraph follows sk1000171 as Check Point revised it on 2026-10-13, with four log indicators.

CISA's ICS advisory ICSA-26-057-10, which this entry said could not be located, lists all 23 identifiers: three missing ones are added (CVE-2026-3037, CVE-2026-22877, CVE-2026-20797), CVE-2026-21718 is typed as the authentication bypass both sources call it, the field-controller link and the register-map wording follow Claroty, the 'zero interaction' claim and the energy sector, which no source supports, are removed, the sourcing note records CISA's CWE for CVE-2026-21718, and the entry is now two-source.

objects.description:
Calendar-invite phishing spreads: Outlook and Gmail add the lure on their own and keep it after the email is deleted

Netcraft reports that phishing lures delivered as ICS calendar files, adopted by widespread campaigns of the EvilTokens Microsoft 365 token-stealing kit, are now spreading to low-effort scams. Outlook with Exchange Online (desktop, web and mobile) and Gmail with Google Calendar add such an invite to the calendar automatically as tentative and keep it after the email is deleted, so purging the message leaves the lure in place. EvilTokens invites posed as meetings, alerts or voicemail and led to a device-code page that has the victim authorise an attacker's device through OAuth; Sublime Security, quoted by The Guardian, reports exponential growth in calendar phishing.
objects.name: Phishing lures sent as ICS calendar invites land in Outlook and Gmail calendars without a click and stay after the email is deleted; EvilTokens used them for Microsoft 365 device-code phishing

objects.description:
OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it

OVHcloud says a hacker used a developer's GitHub account to replace the release binaries of its command-line tool for versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, available for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times; the first replacement was at about 12:47 UTC and OVHcloud deleted the files at 14:21 UTC after a customer's pinned SHA-256 failed. Its postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on the developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue. Anyone who installed or updated the tool from a release asset in that window must rotate every secret on that host; the source tag and the Go module were untouched.

objects.description:

Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) published on 2026-10-19 a technology assessment that sorts authentication methods, tokens and services into the classes tief, mittel and hoch, with a star on mittel and hoch for resistance to real-time phishing. It says methods in class tief, those built on a secret that is the same at every login, should in principle no longer be used. The classification is non-binding and gives no basis for testing or certification; it is a rough guideline from the federal authority for writing authentication requirements.

Three configuration-dependent NGINX heap flaws (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in 1.30.6, 1.31.7 and Debian trixie, not bookworm

The nginx 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) releases of 2026-10-14 fix five security flaws, three of them heap-corruption bugs that F5 scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and an unauthenticated attacker can reach with crafted HTTP requests, but only on configurations that combine alias with rewrite and $request_filename, use a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or enable asynchronous file I/O with server-side includes; the other two concern HTTP/3 and TLS session ticket key rotation. F5 says the heap flaws restart the worker, with code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed; no exploitation or public proof of concept is reported, nginx.org rates all five medium, and Debian fixed trixie with DSA-6575-1 while its bookworm package is still marked vulnerable.

The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, after a honeypot operator documented 35 successful code executions on PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php and VulnCheck extended its working exploit across builds of PHP 8.2 to 8.5; Palo Alto Networks' advisory now reports active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, Dream Research recovered a custom build chained with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that rooted 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and attacked a US government-affiliated network, SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the flaws without naming a CVE, and Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to them. As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.

CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service, Germany's LKA Rheinland-Pfalz and UK law enforcement published advisory AA26-293A on 2026-10-20 on SafePay, which they say was among the most active ransomware groups in 2026 and has affected at least 600 victims, in Europe among other regions. objects.description:
Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; Java needs a second update, and Python, Go, Rust and curl stacks need theirs

On 2026-10-17 a researcher reported that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had been generated with too little randomness, so anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site. Firefox, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft platforms block the intermediates and eMudhra revoked them, but software that keeps its own trust store or does not check revocation stays exposed until updated: Go fixed it in 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 as CVE-2026-111943, Python added a built-in denylist as CVE-2026-115557, and Oracle and OpenJDK's Java update of 2026-10-21 (CVE-2026-91403) was followed on 2026-10-24 by a second alert, CVE-2026-114820 (CVSS 3.1 9.1), that removes four root CAs and that OpenJDK says even a runtime updated in the past few days needs. Chrome removes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root on 2026-10-27; no exploitation is reported.

objects.description: Symantec attributes the HOOKEDGE intrusions to Swallowtail, which it equates with APT28; Recorded Future assesses with moderate confidence that BlueDelta, overlapping APT28, used it

Symantec: APT28's hidden-Edge backdoor hit law-enforcement and defence targets; at a shipbuilder it added an SSH tunnel

Symantec reports that APT28, which it tracks as Swallowtail, used the HOOKEDGE backdoor against a law-enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and a military aircraft-engine manufacturer in two NATO member states, none named. A macro-enabled Word document started a script chain that uses a hidden, off-screen Microsoft Edge window as its HTTP client against a public webhook service; at the shipbuilder the operators then pushed an SSH private key for a persistent tunnel, captured NTLM handshakes from the host itself and ran a previously undocumented in-memory loader, in an intrusion that lasted at least two months. Recorded Future had documented HOOKEDGE against government and diplomatic targets in Romania, Spain and Turkiye in August.

objects.description:
Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them

TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.
objects.name: TeamUpdraft breach: stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys are used to push backdoor plugins to connected WordPress sites, with no flaw in UpdraftPlus and no CVE; deleting the keys is the fix

objects.content: Police authorities, banks, hospitals, schools and prisons are the firm's customers as AWP describes them, not organisations reported in the stolen data; the organisations reported as concerned are judicial entities including the Établissements de la plaine de l'Orbe, gendarmerie premises, several banks and several dozen companies.

Aikido's statement that working Kubernetes proof-of-concept exploits have been published concerns the Dirty Frag family as a whole, not CVE-2026-46300 specifically; the summary and the 2026-09-05 section now attribute it that way, and no source describes a Kubernetes exploit for this CVE. Detection and triage lines are added from Wiz's description of the public exploit and Red Hat's list of legitimate user-namespace uses.

The June dataset figures come from three researchers, and BleepingComputer reports firewall URLs and apparently valid credentials, some confirmed authentic, rather than management URLs and valid credentials: Hudson Rock counted 73,932 URLs in 194 countries and 21,632 domains, Kevin Beaumont put it at about 75,000 devices. SOCRadar's Lynx / INC attribution dates from its 29 June update, while BleepingComputer's October recap dates it to July. The Detection line adds the FBI and Secret Service configuration review, with particular attention to added unrecognized accounts, and the account deletions and password changes they report on compromised devices.

Palo Alto's advisory makes the one-time re-authentication an automatic consequence of the PAN-OS upgrade, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie, not a step to force; the action and the 2026-06-10 and 2026-10-06 sections now say so. The CVE record carries the affected trains and fixed builds from the advisory, and a triage line adds Arctic Wolf's pattern of a cookie decryption failure followed quickly by a successful cookie login.

Code execution was described as possible only with ASLR disabled; depthfirst notes that forked workers share one heap layout that could in theory leak ASLR, and F5's CVE description, updated on 2026-09-10, covers systems where the attacker can bypass ASLR, against NCSC-CH's narrower statement. The headline now names the public proof of concept and VulnCheck's honeypot exploitation attempts, and verbatim quotes from the GitHub advisory, depthfirst, ENISA EUVD and The Hacker News back the trigger, disclosure, ASLR and exploitation statements. A Defender takeaway now names the fixed NGINX Open Source releases and depthfirst's named-capture workaround, replacing the standing action that restated them.

The interim mitigation was given as a module blacklist for every distribution, but Red Hat builds algif_aead into its kernel, where it cannot be blocklisted; Red Hat's boot argument that blocks the affected functions is now given for RHEL, together with Xint's seccomp option and Red Hat's statement that all its fixes are available.

Microsoft does not call Storm-2949 financially motivated: its objective was mass data exfiltration, Storm is a temporary designation, no extortion was seen and there is no ShinyHunters link, and the intrusion was not binary-free, since ScreenConnect was installed on VMs, where a script tried to weaken Defender and to clear event logs. Self-service password reset abuse took over four privileged accounts on a hedged phishing assessment.

objects.description:
LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and in the official images stole cloud and AI credentials; removing the package does not stop it

On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0, the open-source LLM gateway, shipped with malicious Python startup files in all seven PyPI wheels (live 11:39 to 13:23 UTC) and in the official GHCR and Docker Hub images behind the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable tags (11:46 to 14:20 UTC); they run a credential stealer at every Python start and start a background loader that could execute code fetched from an attacker-chosen host, though Socket saw its pointer empty at 13:01 UTC. The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 says a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker, from 2026-10-10, a GitHub organization owner's CLI token, with which it stole two maintainers' tokens and, on 2026-10-21, overrode branch protection to build the release from a look-alike repository; Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running on 2026-10-10. Wiz saw stolen AWS instance-role credentials tested about 4.5 hours after exfiltration; PyPI and the registries removed the release the same day and the maintainers say to pin 1.106.2 or an explicit earlier version.

objects.description: Microsoft: Storm-0940 used ARTEX to automate attacks on hundreds of organizations since at least September 2026

Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique

Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases. Expel independently saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration, enrol Okta Verify and sign in to applications, and CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the same framework. Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer.

objects.description:
Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights

Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date.
objects.name: CVE-2026-114625, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem: an SQL injection lets any authenticated user, down to the Enterprise Read Only role, act as a superuser operator, and Arista says it is actively exploited (CVSS 3.1 9.9)

objects.description:
HPE's Aruba wireless bulletin fixes 19 unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0+; HPE knows of no public exploit code

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 of 2026-10-22 fixes 72 CVEs in AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and access points, 33 of them at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher and 19 of those reachable over the network without authentication (eight at 10.0). HPE found the flaws through internal research, knows of no public discussion or exploit code, and strongly urges patching; its only workaround is to confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated segment behind firewall policy.
objects.name: HPESBNW05162, HPE Networking (Aruba) AOS-8 and AOS-10 wireless: 72 CVEs fixed in one bulletin, 19 of them unauthenticated and network-reachable at CVSS 9.0 or above, across controllers, gateways and access points

objects.description:
NetScaler's PHP2Shell fix is out: 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and FIPS builds; restrict management access until installed

NetScaler Product Security says the two PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect the NetScaler Management Portal, reached through the NSIP GUI, any SNIP that permits management access and the cluster IP GUI, on all supported software versions; NetScaler Console and SVM are not affected. Citrix's bulletin now names the fixed builds, 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS and 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 and later, and tells customers to immediately restrict management access to trusted networks; no source reports an attack on NetScaler, although CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, NetScaler ADC and Gateway: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the management GUI on the NSIP, management-enabled SNIPs and the cluster IP of every supported version; fixed in 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and the FIPS and NDcPP builds

objects.description:
Fortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes for FortiOS and four more products; CVEs wait until 10 November

Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated release of critical and high-severity fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (scheduled for 2026-10-22, after recent FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator releases), found through its AI-assisted testing, and urges every customer to upgrade at once, internet-facing devices first. The CVE advisories follow only on 2026-11-10, so there are no identifiers to triage by; NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown, and the FortiMail builds are the ones that already fix CVE-2026-104286, which Fortinet reports as exploited.
objects.name: Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: critical and high-severity fixes in FortiOS 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 and 7.2.14, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with the advisories withheld until 2026-11-10

objects.description:
Huntress: stolen post-MFA M365 tokens replayed within minutes; a password reset leaves planted devices and MFA methods

Huntress reports that between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-22 it detected 497 Microsoft 365 sign-in events in 79 organizations that replayed tokens stolen through adversary-in-the-middle relays, device-code phishing and social engineering, within minutes of capture and from one rented hosting range. The operators then registered rogue Entra devices, wiped and replaced MFA methods in 19 organizations and hid mail with inbox rules; a password reset alone removes none of it.
objects.name: M365 token spray and replay: Huntress tracks a 10-week campaign that replays stolen post-MFA tokens from rented hosting within minutes, registers rogue Entra devices, wipes and re-registers MFA methods and hides mail with inbox rules of one to three characters or punctuation only

objects.description: Kaspersky GReAT attributes the BlackX campaign to APT41 with medium confidence (curated relation type: attributed-to)

Kaspersky: a UEFI bootkit ran on fully patched Windows because Microsoft's Secure Boot revocation is off by default

Kaspersky GReAT reports BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus that exploits Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker keys and load a kernel driver that blinds security products, installed after attackers held administrator rights on networks of diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan; Kaspersky attributes it to APT41 with medium confidence. The targeted machines were fully patched, because Microsoft's fix revokes the old boot-manager certificate only when an administrator sets a registry flag and runs a scheduled task.
objects.name: BlackX: Kaspersky finds a BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit on fully patched Windows machines of Central Asian diplomatic bodies, because the Baton Drop fix does not revoke the old boot-manager certificate until an administrator triggers it

objects.description:
ESET: a backdoor reaches its C2 through the Yggdrasil mesh; Sandworm wiped the victim two months after UAC-0099 got in

ESET reports that UAC-0099 gained access to a Ukrainian grain logistics company on 2025-07-16 with a spearphishing attachment and a day later deployed MythicRatatoskr, a Go backdoor whose command server sits inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, reached through public peers; on 2025-09-17 the SDelete utility was deployed through Group Policy, which ESET assesses with high confidence as Sandworm after UAC-0099 handed off the access. ESET names blocking the public peer addresses as a viable mitigation.
objects.name: MythicRatatoskr: ESET documents a Go backdoor that hides its command server inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, and a UAC-0099 to Sandworm access handoff that ended in a Group Policy wiper attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics firm

objects.description:
FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed

Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected.
objects.name: Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited

objects.description:
Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now

CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available.

objects.description:
Required LDAP and SMB signing did not stop NTLM relay: a re-authenticated session kept the attacker's key

SpecterOps (LDAP, 2026-10-23) and Blackfield (SMB, 2026-10-21) independently show that a domain controller or file server that requires signing still accepts a relayed NTLM authentication when the attacker first opens a signed session of its own and then re-authenticates it as the victim, so the session keeps a signing key the attacker knows. Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks.
objects.name: NTLM relay past required signing: SpecterOps and Blackfield re-authenticate a signed LDAP or SMB session with a relayed victim identity, and Microsoft fixed it in the September and October 2026 updates

objects.description:

Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative copied public Linux kernel lists on five kernel reports on 2026-10-21 before any fix was merged, and Sysdig ranks ZDI-CAN-33367 as the one to act on: a local privilege escalation through skb_zerocopy() that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with a public exploit that TuxCare reproduced as root on AlmaLinux 8 to 10, CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04. Veeam's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix CVE-2026-108142, an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1 and 13.0 on Windows and of the Veeam Software Appliance (CVSS 4.0 9.1, fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3; 12.x is not affected), a SQL injection in Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 that reaches code execution as the PostgreSQL service account (9.0, fixed in 8.6) and an MFA bypass in Veeam ONE 13.1 for an attacker holding Administrator credentials (8.5). objects.description:
WatchGuard fixes three feature-dependent unauthenticated flaws scored 9.2 in Fireware OS; no exploitation known

WatchGuard's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix 17 flaws in Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and, for T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22, seven of them scored 9.0 or higher. Three need no authentication but a specific feature: a heap write in the Access Portal's WebSocket handling, a stack overflow in the SIP proxy and missing authentication in the FireCluster sync daemon, each scored 9.2. Four more need an attacker who controls or intercepts traffic to an Active Directory server, to WatchGuard Cloud or to a log server. WatchGuard is not aware of exploitation of any of them.
objects.name: WatchGuard Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and 12.5.22: seven of 17 fixed Fireware OS flaws are scored 9.0 or higher, among them unauthenticated memory-corruption and missing-authentication rows in the Access Portal, the SIP proxy and the FireCluster sync daemon; WatchGuard knows of no exploitation

objects.description:
Moldova: unauthenticated e-government services queried for about one million ID numbers; data on 750,000 extracted

Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency says that between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 attackers exploited flaws in state digital services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and, on preliminary estimates, extract data sets for about 750,000 of them, then used what they obtained to extract more from interconnected systems. The Prime Minister says foreign state involvement is being investigated and that AI allegedly helped find the flaws; Moldova has not attributed the attack, and the agency took 82 services under review and disconnected exposed services and more than 30 systems.
objects.name: Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws

objects.description: Leak-site self-claim only: Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that Rhysida listed the municipality's file servers, and the municipality has not confirmed the group or the listing

Machelen municipality: foothold from a website's misleading instructions, 22 days to detection; Rhysida lists its files

The Belgian municipality of Machelen published a timeline in which attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, reached a user with high privileges on 2026-09-10 and were found on 2026-09-11; it confirms that personal data was stolen. Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that the Rhysida group had listed the municipal and social-welfare file servers on its leak site, a claim the municipality has not confirmed.

objects.description:
Huntress: phished MDM enrolments push ScreenConnect back after removal; the RMM is not the root of the intrusion

Huntress reports several recent incidents in which phishing victims ended up with an MDM client from Hexnode or Rippling followed by an unauthorised ScreenConnect agent. In the Rippling case the attacker used the MDM, running with SYSTEM rights, to stage and run ScreenConnect; in the Hexnode case the managed-service provider removed ScreenConnect and it returned several hours later to the same relay while the Hexnode client was still installed. Huntress says the products are not at fault and that removing the RMM does not remove the management architecture behind it.
objects.name: Huntress: phished MDM enrolments in Hexnode and Rippling give attackers a management path that brings ScreenConnect back after it has been removed

objects.description:
ESET: an emailed RAR ran code on MDaemon servers via ClamAV's UnRAR; fixed in MDaemon 26.0.4, ClamAV 1.4.6 and 1.5.4

ESET reports an active campaign in Ukraine in which Russia-aligned attackers exploited MDaemon mail servers: a crafted RAR archive mailed to any address makes MDaemon invoke ClamAV, whose old bundled UnRAR library carries the path-traversal flaw CVE-2025-8088, and the exploit writes a malicious DLL to the server with no user interaction. MDaemon fixed it in 26.0.4 on 2026-08-25, and ClamAV's own notes show that every Windows ClamAV from 0.101.0 to 1.5.3 is affected, fixed in 1.4.6 and 1.5.4. The attackers deployed the HELLAGE mail-stealing backdoor and the Telegram-controlled HELLTAG backdoor.

external_references.source_name: ESET Research (APT Activity Report, April to September 2026)

SafeDep and JFrog: the testmetest npm worm now runs on import, so --ignore-scripts does not stop it; 42 repos armed

SafeDep and JFrog describe an npm worm, tracked as testmetest, whose newest builds start when an application imports the package, so installing with --ignore-scripts does not stop it. It steals SSH, registry, cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials, publishes new patch versions of the victim's own packages, and wipes the home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked. SafeDep counts 19 packages from one operator between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-27; JFrog found 42 armed GitHub repositories of 11 legitimate owners; neither lab names an actor.
objects.name: testmetest: an npm worm in the Miasma and Shai-Hulud family now starts when an application imports the package, so install with --ignore-scripts no longer protects, and JFrog finds 42 third-party GitHub repositories already armed with its publisher

Check Point's advisory sk1000302, last modified 2026-10-29, says the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 9.2 each) can give remote code execution through the web interfaces of Force, Spark and Cloud firewalls that use Mobile Access, SSL Network Extender VPN, SAML-realm VPN authentication, the Identity Awareness captive portal, the UserCheck portal or Zero Phishing. Hotfixes exist for R81.20, R82, R82.10 and R82.20 and for Spark R82.00 and R81.10; the R81.20 package was reissued on 2026-10-28 for gateways that use Mobile Access, and a hotfix for the end-of-support gateway release R81.10 followed on 2026-10-29. The sk makes no statement on exploitation of Check Point products, and CISA lists both flaws as exploited.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Check Point Force, Spark and Cloud firewalls: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the web interfaces of gateways that run Mobile Access, SSL Network Extender, SAML-realm VPN, the Identity Awareness captive portal, UserCheck or Zero Phishing; hotfixes since 2026-10-23, the R81.20 package reissued on 2026-10-28 (CVSS 9.2)

WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory; no source gives a CVE identifier.

Cisco Talos Incident Response's Q3 2026 trends report names public administration, tied with finance at 18 percent of engagements, as the most targeted sector, and puts phishing first and public-facing application exploitation second among initial-access techniques. Its ransomware cases (27 percent of engagements) show help-desk vishing that leads the victim to allow remote access through a legitimate remote-management tool, and operators who uninstall or terminate EDR, including with vulnerable drivers.

privatim, the conference of the Swiss data-protection authorities, revised its guidance on cloud-specific risks for public bodies on 2026-10-02 (version 3.02, replacing the version of 3 February 2022). For particularly sensitive personal data the public body must encrypt with keys only it can use, outsourcing such data or data under a statutory duty of confidentiality to standard SaaS from large international providers is in most cases inadmissible, and the body's top management is to confirm the residual risk in writing.

objects.description:
Drupal Commerce Core access bypass is exploited in the wild; update to 3.3.13 or 8.x-2.41 and audit orders

Drupal's advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254 of 2026-10-28 says an access bypass in the Commerce Core module, which adds a shopping cart and checkout to Drupal sites, is being actively exploited in the wild; the Drupal security team scores it 21 of 25, needing no authentication and affecting every module configuration. Commerce Core 3.0.0 up to but not including 3.3.13, and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41, are affected, and Drupal tells operators to update and audit their orders for inconsistencies. NCSC Switzerland issued its own advisory on 2026-10-30; Drupal says nothing on the method, the actor or the number of sites hit.
objects.name: CVE-2026-118539, Drupal Commerce Core: an access bypass in routes and entity fields is exploited against online stores, fixed in 3.3.13 and 8.x-2.41 (Drupal risk 21 of 25)

objects.description:
Linux TCP use-after-free: Anthropic built a remote root exploit; Ubuntu and RHEL kernels still unfixed

The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. Anthropic reports that Claude wrote an exploit giving a remote, unauthenticated attacker root command execution on servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, and the Go team says the bug is not specific to MPTCP and that Go programs enable MPTCP on Linux listeners by default. Debian's security kernels are fixed while Ubuntu 22.04 to 26.10 and RHEL 8 to 10 had no fixed kernel on 2026-10-30; no source reports public exploit code or attacks.
objects.name: CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners; Debian is fixed, Ubuntu and Red Hat kernels are not yet (CVSS 9.8)

objects.description:
PHP2Shell hits Broadcom endpoint-security servers: App Control 8.12.2 or 8.13.2; SEPM fix builds unconfirmed

Broadcom's Enterprise Security Group advisory 39404, last revised on 2026-10-30, lists Carbon Black App Control Server, Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager (SEPM), the CloudSOC SpanVA Appliance and, since 2026-10-30, Content Analysis and Malware Analysis (CASMA) as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and gives no versions, fixes or workarounds. Broadcom's article 459982 names App Control Server 8.12.2 and 8.13.2 as the fixes for all supported versions; the SEPM builds 14.3.27716.10000 and 14.4.494.0000 rest on a community report that NCSC-NL's tracker accepts, because Broadcom's SEPM advisory needs a login. CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited, and Broadcom's advisory says nothing about attacks on these products.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Broadcom Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager, Carbon Black App Control Server, CloudSOC SpanVA and Content Analysis and Malware Analysis: PHP2Shell reaches the endpoint-security management servers; App Control Server 8.12.2 and 8.13.2 are the fixes Broadcom names

objects.description:
Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor

Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension. Coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor and Sophos say the attacker could not log in there, but the key, the persistence and a host report were still written. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised, and no source says how the attacker published under Anthropic's name.
objects.name: Cursor marketplace: a tampered Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) planted an SSH key, a reverse tunnel and persistence for about eleven hours on 2026-10-29; uninstalling it does not remove the persistence

objects.description:
Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC

Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination.
objects.name: Teams help-desk impersonation to domain-controller identity: Microsoft traces two intrusions from a Quick Assist session to AD CS ESC1 certificates with DCSync, and to PetitPotam relayed to ESC8 Web Enrollment

objects.description:
Progress WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaw can expose admin credentials; fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7

Progress, as CVE numbering authority, published on 2026-10-29 CVE-2026-84295, an improper-authentication flaw in WS_FTP Server on Windows that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker reach administrative credentials (CVSS 3.1 10.0), together with an unauthenticated command injection under certain configurations (CVE-2026-90865, 9.0) and an access-control flaw in the Web Admin console (CVE-2026-90867, 8.1). Builds before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 are affected, and CSIRT Italia counts 6 critical and 3 high flaws in the release and says Progress will issue no patch for unsupported versions. No source reports exploitation, and CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, though a 2023 flaw in the same product is listed with known ransomware use.
objects.name: CVE-2026-84295, Progress WS_FTP Server: an unauthenticated remote authentication flaw can expose administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0), with two more unauthenticated flaws, fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7; no exploitation found
